standards.name: Ecological Metadata Language (EML)
standards.abstract: EML (Ecological Metadata Language) is an XML-schema-based metadata specification designed to describe datasets and data packages commonly produced by observational and experimental research in ecology, earth and environmental sciences. It documents digital (and optionally non-digital) resources using a modular vocabulary that covers bibliographic identification, spatial/temporal/taxonomic coverage, methods and protocols, data structure (entities, attributes, data tables, rasters/vectors), physical file formats, parties (people and organizations), access control, and semantic annotations. The specification is community-maintained (NCEAS/EML project), published as EML 2.2.0, and distributed with normative XML Schema files, documentation, examples, and tooling to validate and produce interoperable EML documents.

classification.rationale: The source material is the EML specification and XML Schema documentation that lists concrete, named metadata modules and elements (e.g., eml, eml-dataset, eml-attribute, eml-dataTable, eml-coverage, etc.). The document presents a structured schema (module/type names and descriptions) rather than only prose guidance or an ordered process. Therefore the source is best represented as a Metadata Table: each named module/element is an independently meaningful field/object in the schema.

eml.name: eml
eml.descr: Top-level wrapper module that contains all metadata content and data-package structure for an EML document.
eml.evidence: The eml module is a wrapper container that allows the inclusion of any metadata content in a single EML document. The eml module is used as a container to hold structured descriptions of ecological resources.

raw_full_info.location: site6 (5.1.1 The eml module - A metadata container)
raw_full_info.quote_context: In EML, the definition of a "Data Package" is the combination of both the data and metadata for a resource. So, data packages are built by using the <eml> wrapper, which will include all of the metadata, and optionally the data (or references to them). All EML packages must begin with the <eml> tag and end with the </eml> tag.

eml-resource.name: eml-resource
eml-resource.descr: Base information common to all resource types (dataset, literature, software, protocol); used as the shared foundation for resource-specific modules.
eml-resource.evidence: The eml-resource module contains general information that describes dataset resources, literature resources, protocol resources, and software resources. Each of the above four types of resources share a common set of information, but also have information that is unique to that particular resource type.

raw_full_info.location: site6 (5.1.2 The eml-resource module - Base information for all resources)
raw_full_info.quote_context: Each resource type uses the eml-resource module to document the information common to all resources, but then extend eml-resource with modules that are specific to that particular resource type.

eml-dataset.name: eml-dataset
eml-dataset.descr: Module for dataset-specific metadata: title, abstract, keywords, contacts, maintenance history, purpose, distribution, and overview of dataset contents.
eml-dataset.evidence: The eml-dataset module contains general information that describes dataset resources. It is intended to provide overview information about the dataset: broad information such as the title, abstract, keywords, contacts, maintenance history, purpose, and distribution of the data
